ei.title: Why You Buy What You Buy

fullPassage: Let’s say you are shopping for a new jacket and the first one you see is priced at $100. That’s too expensive, as you don’t want to spend more than $50. Soon after, you see a similar jacket from a different brand with a $70 price tag. You think it’s ① <u>affordable</u>, even though the price is still beyond your budget. This is because the first piece of information acts as an ② <u>anchor</u> that influences your decisions later. Look at the two pairs of sneakers. They both are $50, but the way their price is presented is different. Naturally, people are more ③ <u>drawn</u> to the second pair. This is because the original price serves as an anchor, making the ④ <u>discounted</u> price appear more ⑤ <u>unreasonable</u> in comparison.

questions.passage: In 2010, Steve Jobs <u>ⓐ introduced</u> the tablet computer to the world. During the presentation, he said, "We’re going to price it under a thousand dollars," <u>ⓑ which</u> most people assumed meant $999. He went on to talk about the features of the tablet and continued <u>ⓒ justifying</u> why the tablet was worth buying. At the end, he said, "I am thrilled <u>ⓓ to announce</u> to you that the pricing starts not at $999 but at just $499." The crowd went wild. He put the $999 price tag in people’s minds at the beginning so that the $499 price <u>ⓔ would seem</u> a lot cheaper in comparison.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 ⓐ~ⓔ 중, 어법상 어색한 것을 고르시오.

det.korean: 그는 이어서 태블릿의 기능에 관해 이야기했고 왜 그것이 구매할 가치가 있는지 계속해서 보여 주었습니다. continue는 to-v와 v-ing 모두 가능하지만, 원문에서는 'continued to justify'가 올바른 표현입니다. 그러나 이 문항에서 'justifying'은 'to justify'로 고쳐야 원문과 일치합니다.
det.analysis: 원문: He went on to talk about the features of the tablet and continued to justify why the tablet was worth buying.
det.tip: 어법 유형 — 지문을 꼼꼼히 읽고 정답을 찾으세요.

questions.passage: In an experiment, one group of students was given a coffee mug and a second group a chocolate bar. Both groups were told they could exchange their items. A third group wasn’t given anything and was told to choose either a chocolate bar or a coffee mug. This group showed an equal preference for the two items. This suggested that roughly half of the first and second groups (A) [would trade / will trade] their items. But that’s not (B) [what / that] happened. Only about 10 percent of the students in the first and second groups were willing to make the exchange. This is because people value something more when they (C) [own / are owned] it.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 (A), (B), (C)에서 어법에 맞는 표현으로 가장 적절한 것을 고르시오.

det.korean: 이는 첫 번째와 두 번째 그룹의 절반 정도가 물건을 교환할 것이라는 걸 암시했습니다. 하지만 그런 일은 일어나지 않았습니다. 사람들이 무언가를 소유했을 때 그것을 더 가치 있게 여기기 때문입니다.
det.analysis: 원문: This suggested that roughly half ~ would trade their items. But that's not what happened. ~ people value something more when they own it.
det.tip: 어법 유형 — 지문을 꼼꼼히 읽고 정답을 찾으세요.

questions.passage: Companies often use the endowment effect as a marketing strategy. For example, many media streaming companies offer free trials to customers. Once customers use the free trial, they feel ownership of that service, even if <u>ⓐ it’s</u> temporary. <u>ⓑ Consequently</u>, they are likely to value it more and are willing to pay to continue <u>ⓒ owning</u> it. A free-return policy is another example. Say that a company is offering free returns on a smartwatch within 30 days of purchase. It seems like a good deal, since you can get a refund even after <u>ⓓ used</u> the item.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 ⓐ~ⓓ 중, 어법상 어색한 것을 고르시오.

det.korean: 제품을 사용한 후에도 환불을 받을 수 있기 때문에 좋은 거래처럼 보입니다. 전치사 after 뒤에는 동명사(v-ing)가 와야 합니다. used(과거형/과거분사)는 전치사의 목적어가 될 수 없으므로 using으로 고쳐야 합니다.
det.analysis: 원문: since you can get a refund even after using the item
det.tip: 어법 유형 — 지문을 꼼꼼히 읽고 정답을 찾으세요.

questions.passage: Do you think that you spend money (A) [wisely / wastefully]? The truth is that most people are not as rational as they think. This is because human beings are easily influenced by (B) [psychological / physical] factors. Steve Jobs used something called the anchoring effect to his advantage. It works because people tend to (C) [rely on / give up] the first piece of information they receive when making decisions.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 (A), (B), (C)에서 문맥에 맞는 낱말로 가장 적절한 것을 고르시오.

det.korean: 돈을 현명하게 쓴다고 생각하나요? 심리적 요인에 쉽게 영향받습니다. 사람들은 처음 접하는 정보에 의존하는 경향이 있습니다.
det.analysis: 원문: Do you think that you spend money wisely? ~ easily influenced by psychological factors. ~ people tend to rely on the first piece of information
det.tip: 어휘 유형 — 지문을 꼼꼼히 읽고 정답을 찾으세요.

det.korean: 할인된 가격을 상대적으로 더 합리적으로 보이게 만들기 때문입니다. 원문은 reasonable(합리적인)인데, ⑤는 unreasonable(비합리적인)로 문맥과 반대되는 의미입니다.

questions.passage: Do you think that you spend money wisely? The truth is that most people are not as rational as they think. det.analysis: 원문: people value something more when they own it
det.tip: 서술 유형 — 지문을 꼼꼼히 읽고 정답을 찾으세요.
